rationale: Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ⲡⲧⲉⲫⲁⲩ (Lyc. orthography for ⲡⲉⲑⲁⲩ 'the evil'). Standard agentive formation paralleling glossary ⲡⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sinner.' Recurs lines 9, 25 — the moral category the Nazorean wrongly applies to the judge.
Lycopolitan orthography for ⲡⲉⲑⲁⲩ/ⲡⲡⲉⲑⲁⲩ 'the evil one/thing.' Double-article form ⲡ-ⲡⲧⲉⲫⲁⲩ recurs throughout this page (lines 3, 12, 14, 31) as the moral object that the judge severs from the man.

ⲥⲁⲛ- prefix from ⲥⲁ- 'side, party' + ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ 'wickedness' yields a categorial-belonging noun: 'one-on-the-side-of-wickedness, partisan of wickedness.' Distinct from ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲫⲁⲩ (active 'doer of evil') — this names the moral classification, not the action. Mani's argument distinguishes acting-against-evil from being-on-the-side-of-evil.

Greek loanword κριτής. The chapter's central term, retained as Greek per the manuscript's preference (cf. accumulated ⲣⲉϩ†ⲍⲉⲡ 'judge' as Coptic equivalent — both attested in this corpus). Capitalized 'Judge' in line 1 and line 30 where applied as divine title to God.
Greek ταυρέα 'bull-hide whip.' First of the three judicial instruments (whip / iron-collar / sword) in the punitive catalogue.
Greek ἑρμητάριον. Punitive instrument paired with the verb ⲧⲙⲱⲣⲉ (τιμωρέω 'punish') — translated functionally as 'punishment-rod' since the precise object (rod, staff, prison) is uncertain.
Latin/Greek κολλάριον 'iron collar, neck-pillory.' The shaming/restraining instrument set upon condemned men.

Greek ναζωραῖος 'Nazorean' (sectarian designation, distinct from the Greek-style ναζαρηνός). In Manichaean polemics designates Jewish-Christian opponents who reject Mani's teaching. The chapter casts him as the foil whose challenge enables the apostolic theodicy.
Greek loanword τιμωρέω 'punish, exact penalty.' Standard judicial-punitive verb in the four-verb series (beats / punishes / slays / kills).
ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲉ = ⲡⲉⲧ-ⲉⲓⲣⲉ 'the one who does' + ⲛⲧⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ 'the wickedness.' Substantival relative paralleling ⲡⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sinner' but more emphatically punctual: the actual perpetrator of a wicked act.

Substantival qualitative ⲡⲉⲧ- + ⲥⲙⲁⲁⲛⲧ (= Sah. ⲥⲙⲟⲛⲧ 'be established'). 'That which is rightly set, the established right' — pair-partner with ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϥⲣⲉ 'the goodness' in the moral inventory of the rewarded act.
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲛⲁϥⲣⲉ (= ⲛⲟϥⲣⲉ 'good thing,' already in glossary). Names the moral-substantial good which earns its recompense, antithetical to ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ 'wickedness.'
ⲃⲏⲙⲁ (Greek βῆμα 'judgment-seat, tribunal'). Standard juridical architectural term for the locus of judgment — the place beside which free good men stand without fear.
